title: One round advances the counts
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $y$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $t$ be a natural number. If $b$ is a Boolean tag that correctly marks the boundary whenever the input head is at either boundary position in the configuration reached after $t$ steps on $y$, then advancing the counts at time $t$ using the machine's displacements computed with tag $b$ gives exactly the counts at time $t+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$b$ is a Boolean tag satisfying the boundary-tag condition for the input-head position at time $t$
replaced: For every source machine, virtual input $y$, time $t$, and valid tag $b$ for the position reached at time $t$, advancing the counts at time $t$ by the displacements computed from $b$ yields exactly the counts at time $t+1$.
